subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Midnight's Children and Postcolonial Magic
description: A micro-lesson that makes Midnight's Children and Postcolonial Magic usable.

hook.text: Salman Rushdie wrote a novel where a child born at midnight on India's independence gains magical powers.

buildup.text: Midnight's Children followed one thousand and one children all born in India's first hour of freedom.

discovery.text: Published in 1981, it blended magical realism with Indian history to tell a nation's story through one boy.

twist.text: Rushdie later faced death threats for another novel but said Midnight's Children was the one he lived for.

climax.text: The novel won the Booker Prize and was twice voted the best Booker winner in the prize's entire history.

punchline.text: A nation's birth was told through a child's magic.

quiz.question: What special distinction did Midnight's Children receive?
options: It was the longest Booker Prize nominee
It was twice voted the best Booker winner in the prize's history
It was the first novel published in India
